grades.bullseye: Sincere, clean, family-pitched hate-watch; nobody involved is joking
grades.rough: Fun but crude or grimy enough to get in the way (Gunda's tier)
grades.knowing: Winks at itself; self-aware camp, the riskiest tier
grades.sequel: Franchise extension; the untested sequel hypothesis

categories.name: The launch
categories.blurb: A production house spends real money introducing a new face. Somebody's whole career is riding on it, so nobody involved is joking for a single frame. Glossy, clean, aspirational, enormous soundtrack, no writing at all. This is your densest cluster by a wide margin.

categories.name: The campus film
categories.blurb: Youth, friendship, first love, a soundtrack that outlives the film, and dialogue nobody proofread. Shot like an advertisement for being nineteen.

categories.name: The vanity project
categories.blurb: The person with the money cast themselves, or their own comeback, in the lead. The sincerity is total because the film is an argument about their own worth.

categories.name: Melodrama at the wrong volume
categories.blurb: Family, duty, sacrifice and weeping, pitched so high it becomes comedy without ever intending to. Clean enough to watch with anyone's parents, which is part of why it works.

categories.name: The sincere ghost story
categories.blurb: Hindi horror has never once winked. The scares miss, which converts the whole thing to comedy, and the songs reset the pacing every twenty minutes so you never hit a slog.

categories.name: The spectacle that cost too much
categories.blurb: Someone was given the largest budget in the industry and complete creative freedom at the same time. The result is enormous, immaculate-looking and makes no sense, and everyone involved was certain it would change cinema.

categories.name: Fast and stupid
categories.blurb: No category, no theme, just incident. Something happens every ninety seconds and none of it follows from anything else. The only hard requirement on this whole list is that it never slows down.

categories.name: Imports
categories.blurb: The same rule, elsewhere. Everything here is short, sincere and relentless, and none of it is trying to be funny.

categories.name: The South remake
categories.blurb: A Telugu or Tamil hit rebuilt in Hindi. The plot crosses over intact and the texture does not: what made the original land was a place, a star and an audience that already agreed, and none of that is portable. What is left is pure formula delivered with total conviction, which is exactly your zone.

categories.name: The sincere beat-'em-up
categories.blurb: A martial-arts revenge film with real emotional stakes played completely straight. A dead parent, a stolen girl, a training montage, and a hero who never once suggests any of it is silly. The fight choreography is usually genuinely good, which makes the earnestness around it land even harder.

categories.name: Place as a character
categories.blurb: An ensemble stuck in one house, one village, one week. The setting is not a backdrop, it is the plot. Funny and sad in the same shot, and nobody in it is glamorous.

categories.name: A nobody in over his head
categories.blurb: An ordinary man makes one bad decision and the film tightens around him. Plotted like a watch, funny in a deadpan way, and usually set somewhere specific and unfashionable.

categories.name: Money decides everything
categories.blurb: Class is the engine, not the theme. Somebody wants access to something they cannot afford, and the film is honest about what that costs. No speeches.

categories.name: Horror that works
categories.blurb: Same genre as category five, opposite intent. Several of these are among the best films India has made in any register.

categories.name: Both lists at once
categories.blurb: Genuinely excellent films entirely about the thing you two keep doing on purpose. If you only watch three things off this page, make it these.

films.title: Heropanti
films.note: Tiger's debut, built from the ground up to launch him. A reviewer at the time called it a shoddy launch; you called it a good night.

films.title: Main Tera Hero
films.note: Varun's second, directed by his father. Loud, clean, completely without irony.

films.title: Yaariyan
films.note: Divya Khosla Kumar's first film as director. Panned everywhere; the album was inescapable for a year.

films.title: Student of the Year
films.note: The original: Karan Johar launching three faces at once. You were already there.

films.title: Loveshhuda
films.note: Girish Kumar's relaunch after Ramaiya Vastavaiya. His father tried twice.

films.title: Ishaqzaade
films.note: Arjun Kapoor's launch, and the shoutiest romance of its year.

films.title: Hero
films.note: Salman launching Sooraj Pancholi and Athiya Shetty. Enormous money, total conviction, no result.

films.title: Loveyatri
films.note: Salman launching his brother-in-law. The sincerity here is almost uncomfortable.

films.title: Tadap
films.note: Milan Luthria launching Ahan Shetty. Glossy, shouty, played dead straight.

films.title: Mirzya
films.note: Rakeysh Omprakash Mehra launching Harshvardhan Kapoor with a lavish mythic epic. Nobody came.

films.title: Dhadak
films.note: Janhvi's launch, remaking Sairat and missing everything that made Sairat work. Instructive to watch both.

films.title: Sanam Teri Kasam
films.note: Flopped hard, then became a real cult rewatch. Sincere to the point of pain.

films.title: Khaali Peeli
films.note: Ishaan and Ananya in a Mumbai night-chase. Earnest and completely inert.

films.title: Nadaaniyan
films.note: Ibrahim Ali Khan's launch. Critics savaged it, but it sits squarely in the Student of the Year 2 lineage.

films.title: Dishkiyaoon
films.note: A Shilpa Shetty production relaunching Harman Baweja. Third time, same conviction.

films.title: Prem Aggan
films.note: Feroz Khan launching his son. The ancestor of everything in this category.

films.title: Love Story 2050
films.note: A father, a son, and a time machine. Songs, a robot, and absolute belief.

films.title: Machine
films.note: Abbas-Mustan launching their nephew. The purest specimen of the form.

films.title: Victory
films.note: Harman Baweja plays a cricketer. Sincere, clean, forgotten by everyone including the makers.

films.title: Drona
films.note: Abhishek relaunched as a superhero. Total conviction, zero plot.

films.title: Kalank
films.note: Not a launch, but the same glossy sincerity collapsing at enormous scale.

films.title: Krishna Cottage
films.note: The film that started this whole conversation. Campus first, curse second.

films.title: Kuch To Hai
films.note: The closest sibling Krishna Cottage has. Campus, curse, songs, Esha Deol. Do this one.

films.title: Pyaar Impossible
films.note: Uday Chopra wrote himself a romance with Priyanka Chopra. A campus film and a vanity project at once.

films.title: Befikre
films.note: Aditya Chopra's sincere attempt at modern youth romance. Mocked relentlessly, meant entirely.

films.title: Sixteen
films.note: Delhi teenagers, handled with total gravity and no understanding of teenagers.

films.title: Jawani Diwani
films.note: Emraan Hashmi campus comedy. Exactly the mid-2000s texture you keep returning to.

films.title: Love Aaj Kal
films.note: Imtiaz Ali remaking his own film and getting destroyed for it. He meant every word.

films.title: Ishq Vishk Rebound
films.note: A recent launch-plus-campus double. The formula is alive and unchanged.

films.title: Aap Kaa Surroor
films.note: The one that started your Himesh run, and still the clearest case of the type.

films.title: Karzzzz
films.note: Dies, reincarnates as a globally famous rockstar. Obviously.

films.title: The Xpose
films.note: Himesh as a 1960s superstar detective. He believed it.

films.title: Mrityudaata
films.note: Amitabh's own company producing his comeback. Sooryavansham's immediate neighbour and even more earnest. Your next watch.

films.title: Veer
films.note: Salman wrote this period epic himself, and every scene carries the weight of that decision.

films.title: Jaadugar
films.note: Amitabh as a con-man godman. Notorious even among his flops.

films.title: Sooryavansham
films.note: Your calibration point for this entire half of the list.

films.title: Suryavamsam
films.note: The Telugu original Sooryavansham remade. Worth seeing the source.

films.title: Baghban
films.note: Weaponised parental guilt, delivered with absolute conviction. The purest one after Sooryavansham.

films.title: Baabul
films.note: Same director, now on widow remarriage. Same sincerity, same shamelessness.

films.title: Lal Baadshah
films.note: Same year as Sooryavansham, same register, double role, no winking.

films.title: Kohram
films.note: Amitabh and Nana Patekar in a sequence of disguises, played entirely straight.

films.title: Ab Tumhare Hawale Watan Saathiyo
films.note: Four hours of patriotic melodrama. Clean to a fault. Split it over two nights.

films.title: Yaadein
films.note: Subhash Ghai genuinely believed this was a masterpiece about family values. 4.2 on IMDb.

films.title: Pardes
films.note: Ghai NRI melodrama at maximum pitch. India good, America bad, extremely loudly.

films.title: Kisna
films.note: Ghai's period epic. Sincere, lavish, completely inert.

films.title: Yuvvraaj
films.note: Ghai again: Salman, classical music, Austria. Baffling and entirely heartfelt.

films.title: Raja Hindustani
films.note: Peak-nineties melodrama. The slaps, the songs, the shouting, the rain.

films.title: Khuda Gawah
films.note: Operatic to the point of delirium. Amitabh in Afghanistan, shouting beautifully.

films.title: Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna
films.note: Three hours of wealthy misery. Divisive; a lot of people find it hysterical.

films.title: Saawariya
films.note: Bhansali's blue-lit catastrophe. Genuinely beautiful and genuinely insane.

films.title: What's Your Raashee?
films.note: Priyanka plays twelve characters across three and a half entirely sincere hours.

films.title: Saawan: The Love Season
films.note: A legendarily bad romance with no crudeness and no idea what it is doing.

films.title: Dil Diya Hai
films.note: Abbas-Mustan romance-thriller, straight-faced from the first frame.

films.title: Jaan-E-Mann
films.note: Stylised, strange, utterly heartfelt, and a total flop. Akshay plays an astronaut.

films.title: Yeh Dil Aashiqana
films.note: A debut wrapped in a sincere romance nobody remembers. Pure 2000s texture.

films.title: Hero: Love Story of a Spy
films.note: Sunny Deol, enormous production, enormous conviction, no self-awareness anywhere.

films.title: Tere Naam
films.note: Sincere about an obsession it mistakes for romance. The violence gets genuinely ugly.

films.title: Raaz
films.note: Vikram Bhatt. The film that started the wave Krishna Cottage belongs to.

films.title: Vaastu Shastra
films.note: Krishna Cottage's exact contemporary. Haunted bungalow, creepy child, total conviction.

films.title: Naina
films.note: Urmila in a remake of The Eye. Deeply silly and completely straight.
Vikram Bhatt period possession. The sequels get worse, which is a feature.

films.title: Shaapit
films.note: Bhatt at his most notorious. 160 minutes of curse, no irony anywhere.

films.title: Mr. X
films.note: Bhatt doing the invisible man. Sincere and very silly.

films.title: Agyaat
films.note: RGV jungle monster film in which the monster is essentially never shown.

films.title: Darna Mana Hai
films.note: RGV anthology. Segment quality swings violently, which is the appeal.

films.title: Chandramukhi 2
films.note: The bad sequel to a good film. Watch Manichitrathazhu first to feel the drop.

films.title: Nagina
films.note: Sridevi as a shape-shifting naagin, plus the Main Teri Dushman dance-off.

films.title: Purana Mandir
films.note: The Ramsay Brothers' biggest hit, and the demon Samri. Start the Ramsay run here.

films.title: Bandh Darwaza
films.note: Dracula in a Rajasthani haveli. The vampire is named Neola. Goofy, not grimy.

films.title: Mahakaal
films.note: An unlicensed Nightmare on Elm Street with a Michael Jackson-impersonating sidekick.

films.title: 3D Saamri
films.note: Shot in actual 3D. In 1985. On a Ramsay budget.

films.title: Veerana
films.note: The Ramsay cult favourite, and much the leeriest of them.

films.title: Jaani Dushman: Ek Anokhi Kahani
films.note: A 300-year-old snake-man and fifteen stars. Goes leery in stretches.

films.title: Raaz 3
films.note: 3D, black magic, cockroaches. Vamps harder than it haunts.

films.title: Creature 3D
films.note: Bipasha versus a CGI Brahmarakshas. Sleazier than it needs to be.

films.title: Hisss
films.note: A naagin film David Lynch's daughter directed and then disowned. Also quite leery.

films.title: Darna Zaroori Hai
films.note: The sequel anthology. A couple of segments start winking, which dulls it.

films.title: Ajooba
films.note: Amitabh's mother is a dolphin. A crab monster unchains him. The finale has demons and donkeys.

films.title: Ra.One
films.note: SRK being completely sincere about a superhero he believed in. Clean, family, songs.

films.title: Blue
films.note: Akshay underwater, a Kylie Minogue song, and the biggest budget in India at the time.

films.title: Krrish 3
films.note: Rakesh Roshan meant all of it. Family-pitched, zero shame, enormous.

films.title: Thugs of Hindostan
films.note: Vast, costly, earnest, and inert. The modern Kisna.

films.title: Shamshera
films.note: A sincere period epic collapsing under its own costume budget.

films.title: Bade Miyan Chote Miyan
films.note: Akshay and Tiger, played with total gravity. Recent enough to feel current.
Rajinikanth versus a bird-man played by Akshay Kumar. Huge, clean, insane.

films.title: Kochadaiiyaan
films.note: Rajinikanth in motion-capture animation. Nightmarish and entirely in earnest.

films.title: Lingaa
films.note: Rajinikanth builds a dam. Sincere, long, and a famous disaster.

films.title: Indian 2
films.note: Shankar's enormous collapse, twenty-eight years on. Sincere, but still a sequel.

films.title: Saaho
films.note: Prabhas. Incoherent on a scale that requires real belief to achieve.

films.title: Radhe Shyam
films.note: Prabhas as a celebrity palmist. Lavish, operatic, universally mocked, completely sincere.

films.title: Akhanda
films.note: Balakrishna and Boyapati Srinu. The most sincere film ever made about a man with dreadlocks.

films.title: Akhanda 2
films.note: On 2025 worst-of lists as the meme-watchable kind. A sequel though, so unproven for you.

films.title: Gunda
films.note: You liked it. Noted as the ceiling: the rhyming couplets are perfect, the rest is a lot.

films.title: Taarzan: The Wonder Car
films.note: A man dies, reincarnates as a car, the car takes revenge. Abbas-Mustan found this moving.

films.title: Mard
films.note: Manmohan Desai. Amitabh has MARD branded onto his chest in the first reel.

films.title: Chandni Chowk to China
films.note: Akshay Kumar, a Chinese village, and a vegetable cutter with a destiny.

films.title: Race 3
films.note: Our business is our business, none of your business. Meme-dense and dead serious.

films.title: Roar: Tigers of the Sundarbans
films.note: A CGI tiger revenge thriller. The tiger has motivation.

films.title: Radhe
films.note: Short, clean, and Salman believes every frame of it.

films.title: Sikandar
films.note: An organ-donation plot nobody saw coming, least of all the writers.

films.title: War 2
films.note: The leads' unintended chemistry became its own genre of post. Franchise sequel, so unproven.

films.title: Teri Baaton Mein Aisa Uljha Jiya
films.note: A robot romance played with a completely straight face. Clean and odd.

films.title: Joker
films.note: Akshay, aliens, a village of lunatics. Shirish Kunder keeps nudging you, which costs it.

films.title: Himmatwala
films.note: Fast and loud, but Sajid Khan is winking and crude. Lower priority than it looks.

films.title: Birdemic: Shock and Terror
films.note: The horror equivalent of The Room. The birds are animated GIFs. Entirely sincere.

films.title: Miami Connection
films.note: A synth-rock taekwondo band versus cocaine ninjas. Earnest about friendship. Wholesome, actually.

films.title: Troll 2
films.note: Still the peak. Chase it with the documentary Best Worst Movie.

films.title: Night of the Lepus
films.note: Giant killer rabbits, played by actual rabbits filmed in slow motion.

films.title: The Giant Claw
films.note: The monster is a string-operated bird puppet with an expression of mild concern.

films.title: Plan 9 from Outer Space
films.note: Ed Wood's masterpiece, and 79 minutes, so there is no slog risk at all.

films.title: Shocker
films.note: Wes Craven's own misfire. The killer travels through television signals.

films.title: Deadly Friend
films.note: Craven again. A robot friend, and a basketball used for decapitation.

films.title: Silent Night, Deadly Night Part 2
films.note: Forty minutes of recycled footage, then it produces GARBAGE DAY.

films.title: Turkish Star Wars
films.note: It simply uses stolen Star Wars footage and hopes nobody notices.

films.title: The Happening
films.note: Mark Wahlberg versus plants, for 91 unbroken and humourless minutes.

films.title: The Wicker Man
films.note: Nicolas Cage. The bees. Played absolutely straight by everyone involved.

films.title: Jaws: The Revenge
films.note: Michael Caine never saw it, but he has seen the house it paid for.

films.title: The Room
films.note: The canonical text. Skip past the sex scenes and it is perfect.

films.title: Samurai Cop
films.note: The wig, the dialogue, the continuity. Gets crude in patches.

films.title: Hard Ticket to Hawaii
films.note: A skateboard, a blow-up doll and a bazooka in one shot. Very much a lot.

films.title: Riki-Oh: The Story of Ricky
films.note: Gore physics from another dimension. Far past the Gunda line.

films.title: Ramaiya Vastavaiya
films.note: Prabhu Deva directing a producer's son in his own father's film. A launch and a remake at once, which is why it works on you twice over.

films.title: R... Rajkumar
films.note: Prabhu Deva and Shahid Kapoor, the same year. Notorious, loud, played completely straight.

films.title: Action Jackson
films.note: Prabhu Deva and Ajay Devgn. One of the great sincere Hindi disasters of the decade.

films.title: Policegiri
films.note: Sanjay Dutt remaking Saamy. Earnest, loud, forgotten within a fortnight.

films.title: Tevar
films.note: Arjun Kapoor remaking Okkadu. Every beat intact, every reason for the beats missing.

films.title: It's Entertainment
films.note: Akshay Kumar loses an inheritance to a dog. Family-pitched and absolutely sincere.

films.title: Jai Ho
films.note: Salman remaking the Telugu Stalin. A chain-of-kindness premise, delivered at full volume.

films.title: Khiladi 786
films.note: Akshay, Himesh on the soundtrack, and a wedding-broker plot nobody can summarise.

films.title: Singh Is Bliing
films.note: Prabhu Deva and Akshay once more. The formula on autopilot, still fully committed.

films.title: Gabbar Is Back
films.note: Akshay remaking Ramanaa as a vigilante lecture. Sincere to the point of sermon.

films.title: Rowdy Rathore
films.note: Prabhu Deva and Akshay remaking Vikramarkudu. The one that actually worked, so watch it to see the difference.

films.title: Baaghi
films.note: You loved it. Kalaripayattu, a dead master, a kidnapped girl, and not one wink in 134 minutes.

films.title: Munna Michael
films.note: Sabbir Khan and Tiger a third time, now about a Michael Jackson impersonator. The last unwatched film in that pairing, so do this first.

films.title: A Flying Jatt
films.note: Tiger as a reluctant superhero fighting a man made of pollution. Family-pitched and deranged.

films.title: Commando
films.note: Vidyut Jammwal's launch. Real Kalaripayattu, no stunt double, zero irony. The closest thing to Baaghi's register.

films.title: Junglee
films.note: Vidyut and a herd of elephants, directed by the man who made The Mask. Utterly sincere.

films.title: Khuda Haafiz
films.note: Vidyut crossing a border to rescue his wife. Rescue melodrama at full emotional volume.

films.title: Force
films.note: Vidyut's breakout as the villain opposite John Abraham. A Tamil remake, played dead straight.

films.title: Rocky Handsome
films.note: John Abraham remaking The Man from Nowhere. Grim, sincere, and much better choreographed than it needed to be.

films.title: Satyameva Jayate
films.note: John Abraham burning corrupt policemen alive, as a public service. Completely humourless.

films.title: Shivaay
films.note: Ajay Devgn directing himself up a mountain. A vanity project and a beat-'em-up at once.

films.title: Ganapath
films.note: Tiger in a dystopia nobody explains. Clean, loud, sincerely incoherent.

films.title: Heropanti 2
films.note: Sabbir Khan and Tiger eight years on. A famous disaster, but it is a sequel, so treat it as a test of the rule below.

films.title: Baaghi 2
films.note: Different director, bigger budget, and the first one's reputation doing the work.

films.title: Baaghi 3
films.note: Tiger single-handedly invades Syria. Nobody blinks, but by now the series knows what it is.

films.title: Monsoon Wedding
films.note: Your benchmark. Everything below is chasing this.

films.title: Thithi
films.note: Kannada, cast with non-actors from the real village. The closest Indian film to The Pool.

films.title: Ee.Ma.Yau
films.note: A funeral in a coastal village slides into farce and then grief. Start your Lijo run here.

films.title: Kumbalangi Nights
films.note: Four brothers in a Kochi backwater. Fahadh Faasil is genuinely frightening.

films.title: A Death in the Gunj
films.note: A family holiday curdling over a week in 1979. Monsoon Wedding's shape, much colder.

films.title: Gamak Ghar
films.note: A house in Bihar across three decades. Slow, textural, close to perfect.

films.title: Aattam
films.note: A theatre troupe, one allegation, twelve men arguing. National Award winner.

films.title: Jallikattu
films.note: A buffalo escapes and the village loses its mind. Lijo again, at full tilt.

films.title: Laapataa Ladies
films.note: Warm, funny, and considerably sharper than its poster suggests.

films.title: Ankhon Dekhi
films.note: A Chandni Chowk man decides to believe only what he has seen himself.

films.title: Bhooter Bhabishyat
films.note: Bengali. Ghosts from different eras squatting in a Kolkata mansion. Very funny.

films.title: Salaam Bombay!
films.note: More Mira Nair, thirteen years before Monsoon Wedding.

films.title: Manorama Six Feet Under
films.note: Small-town Rajasthan, a clerk who cannot afford to be a hero. One of your two anchors.

films.title: Andhadhun
films.note: The other anchor. A black farce that never once loses its footing.

films.title: Johnny Gaddaar
films.note: Sriram Raghavan before Andhadhun, and his best film. Watch this one first, ahead of everything.

films.title: Aaranya Kaandam
films.note: Tamil one-day gangster noir. Funny, vicious, beautifully controlled.

films.title: Jigarthanda
films.note: A film student tries to make a gangster movie about a real gangster. Funny, then very not.

films.title: Maqbool
films.note: Macbeth in the Bombay underworld. For the Wasseypur half of your sofa.

films.title: Super Deluxe
films.note: Tamil. Four stories, one day, absolute formal control.

films.title: Titli
films.note: A Delhi carjacking family. Brutal; only when you are both up for it.

films.title: The Pool
films.note: Chris Smith in Panjim. Your most unusual favourite, and the key to this category.

films.title: Gangs of Wasseypur
films.note: Your friend's favourite. Coal, revenge and inflation across three generations.

films.title: Is Love Enough? Sir
films.note: The Pool's exact class dynamic, moved into a Mumbai high-rise. Watch this next.

films.title: Kaaka Muttai
films.note: Two slum kids want to eat a pizza. Funny for an hour, then devastating.

films.title: The Great Indian Kitchen
films.note: Domestic labour shot like horror. Quietly, enormously furious.

films.title: Masaan
films.note: Varanasi, class, grief. If you want the emotional one, it is this.

films.title: Court
films.note: Chaitanya Tamhane. Deadpan, procedural, quietly one of the best.

films.title: Khosla Ka Ghosla
films.note: Dibakar Banerjee. A Delhi family against a property shark.

films.title: Oye Lucky! Lucky Oye!
films.note: Dibakar again. A Delhi thief's life told as picaresque comedy.

films.title: Visaranai
films.note: Police custody, unglamorously. Hard to watch and impossible to forget.

films.title: Pariyerum Perumal
films.note: Caste inside a Tamil law college. Patient, then devastating.

films.title: Mukkabaaz
films.note: Boxing and caste in UP. Kashyap's warmest film by a distance.

films.title: All We Imagine as Light
films.note: Two Mumbai nurses. Won the Grand Prix at Cannes and deserves it.

films.title: Sairat
films.note: Marathi. The last twenty seconds will stay with both of you for years.

films.title: The Lunchbox
films.note: The gentle one, for a night when nobody wants to be wrecked.

films.title: Tumbbad
films.note: Folk horror about a cursed god and three generations of greed. Gorgeous and mean. Start here.

films.title: Manichitrathazhu
films.note: Malayalam. The original Chandramukhi, and far better. Shobana is extraordinary.

films.title: Bramayugam
films.note: Black and white, Mammootty as a sinister patriarch in a forest mansion.

films.title: Bhoothakaalam
films.note: Malayalam. Grief as a haunting, almost entirely inside one flat.

films.title: Kaun
films.note: RGV directing an Anurag Kashyap script. One house, three people, ninety minutes.

films.title: Raat
films.note: RGV's genuinely frightening one, made before he started enjoying himself.

films.title: Gehrayee
films.note: A possession film that takes the family's class panic as seriously as the ghost.

films.title: Woh Kaun Thi?
films.note: The great Hindi gothic. Sadhana, fog, and Naina Barse. Still eerie.

films.title: Madhumati
films.note: Bimal Roy doing reincarnation with real craft. The template everything copied.

films.title: Pizza
films.note: Tamil. Karthik Subbaraj's cheap, clever, excellent haunted-house film.

films.title: Stree
films.note: The horror comedy that lands, and a sharp joke about small-town men.

films.title: House
films.note: Japanese. A girl eaten by a piano, a flying severed head. Insane on purpose and brilliant.

films.title: American Movie
films.note: Chris Smith, same man as The Pool, on a broke Wisconsin guy making a terrible horror short. Sundance Grand Jury Prize.

films.title: Ed Wood
films.note: The worst director who ever lived, filmed with enormous affection. Pair it with Plan 9.

films.title: Amar Akbar Anthony
films.note: Manmohan Desai. Completely unhinged and genuinely great at once. The transfusion scene.

didnt_land.title: Kaal
didnt_land.note: Slick, self-conscious, MTV-styled, with an item number winking at the camera. Glossy, not sincere.

didnt_land.title: Kaalo
didnt_land.note: Grimy and mean rather than earnest. The same end of the scale as the roughest Ramsay films.

didnt_land.title: Badass Ravi Kumar
didnt_land.note: Himesh in on the joke, in a spin-off trading on his meme. His other films work because he is not.

didnt_land.title: Student of the Year 2
didnt_land.note: A sequel leaning on the first film's memory, with an established star and a knowing tone. The original was a sincere launch; this is a franchise extension.

do_not_watch.title: Humshakals
